records.horticulturalType: Melissa officinalis species identity; no named cultivar assigned

Kew accepts T. majus and T. minus as species but does not identify this cultivar. Keep species null pending cultivar-level resolution.

records.horticulturalType: Species-level tropical foliage houseplant; cultivar unspecified

conflicts: Johnny's groups several cress species in one growing guide; the crop-type schedule used here is specifically its Wrinkled Crinkled Cress entry, not a cultivar assigned to this identity.

records.horticulturalType: Species-level perennial edible common/garden sorrel; not French sorrel or red-veined sorrel

records.horticulturalType: Species-level edible Malabar spinach; distinct from ornamental Basella rubra; cultivar unspecified
conflicts: UF/IFAS uses Basella cordifolia as a synonym of B. alba in its crop guide; the canonical accepted name follows Kew POWO. UF/IFAS also distinguishes ornamental B. rubra, which is not represented here.

records.horticulturalType: Accepted subspecies / yardlong-bean crop group within Vigna unguiculata; cultivar unspecified
conflicts: Long bean is treated as Vigna unguiculata subsp. sesquipedalis by POWO and NC State; UF/IFAS uses the crop name long bean. It remains distinct from common bean and is not treated as a separate species from cowpea.

records.horticulturalType: Species-level bitter-melon crop; Chinese and Indian horticultural types not resolved to a named selection
conflicts: UF/IFAS distinguishes Chinese and Indian horticultural types with different fruit characteristics; the identity is species-level and does not assign either type. UF/IFAS ecological caution is Florida-specific.

records.horticulturalType: Species-level cultivated peanut; runner, Spanish, Virginia, and Valencia types not selected
conflicts: UF/IFAS and Iowa State report materially different sowing-depth ranges; the seed profile preserves the conflict and directs users to current local packet or Extension instructions instead of inventing a single value. Iowa State warns its 1997 article may be outdated.

records.horticulturalType: Species-level edible common purslane; distinct from ornamental Portulaca grandiflora; cultivar unspecified
conflicts: Common purslane is also treated as a persistent weed; UF/IFAS and UW Extension distinguish it from ornamental moss rose (P. grandiflora). Named upright crop cultivars mentioned by UW Extension are not assigned to this species-level identity.

records.horticulturalType: Species-level smooth luffa; distinct from angled luffa (Luffa acutangula); cultivar unspecified
conflicts: Kew accepts Luffa aegyptiaca and lists L. cylindrica as a synonym; UF/IFAS uses both names for smooth luffa and distinguishes angled luffa as L. acutangula. No named cultivar is represented.

records.horticulturalType: Species-level warm-season leafy crop commonly called New Zealand spinach; distinct from Spinacia oleracea
conflicts: POWO accepts Tetragonia tetragonoides and treats T. expansa as a synonym; older horticultural references may use T. expansa. The common name does not indicate botanical relationship to true spinach.

records.horticulturalType: Sweet-corn crop type within Zea mays; cultivar and sugary genotype unspecified
conflicts: Sweet-corn kernel-genetic classes differ in cold-soil sensitivity; Utah State Extension and UMN Extension give different planting-soil thresholds (60°F versus 65°F for untreated seed). The profile retains their scope and does not select a cultivar or genotype.

records.horticulturalType: Species-level edible sweetpotato; ornamental foliage cultivars not assigned
conflicts: Sweetpotato is botanically distinct from Solanum tuberosum. Common English usage sometimes calls it yam, but this record does not represent Dioscorea species or a named sweetpotato cultivar.

records.horticulturalType: Species-level cultivated potato; no cultivar, market class or subspecies selected
conflicts: Solanum tuberosum includes a very large cultivar diversity and historically treated names/synonyms. No cultivar or subspecies is selected. Home-garden “seed potatoes” are tubers, not botanical seed.

records.horticulturalType: Rose of Sharon species identity; cultivar unspecified

records.horticulturalType: Common staghorn fern species; epiphytic fern, not a seed plant

records.horticulturalType: Delta maidenhair fern species; no named cultivar

records.horticulturalType: Scarlet star bromeliad species; no bract-color cultivar assigned

records.horticulturalType: Thanksgiving cactus species; distinct from the Christmas cactus hybrid S. × buckleyi

records.horticulturalType: Arabian jasmine species; flower form and cultivar unspecified

records.horticulturalType: Areca palm species; dwarf cultivars not specified
conflicts: Retail areca palms may be selected cultivars; no cultivar is established for this species-level identity.

records.horticulturalType: Norfolk Island pine species; no cultivar assigned
conflicts: Despite its common name, this species is not a true pine in Pinus.

records.horticulturalType: Nerve plant species; leaf-vein color form and cultivar unspecified
conflicts: Retail plants may be selected for different vein colors or dwarf form; no named cultivar or color form is assigned.

records.horticulturalType: Sweetheart plant species; sold leaf-only products do not establish a complete vine or cultivar
conflicts: Retail heart-shaped leaf products may lack a node and fail to develop a vine; product form is not treated as a distinct identity.

records.horticulturalType: Rattlesnake plant species; no cultivar assigned
conflicts: Older horticultural sources may use Calathea lancifolia; Kew's accepted name is Goeppertia insignis.

records.horticulturalType: Watermelon peperomia species; no cultivar assigned
conflicts: Common names vary; accepted spelling argyraea is retained rather than the horticultural variant argyreia.

records.horticulturalType: Lipstick plant species; no cultivar assigned
conflicts: The trade name Lipstick Plant may cover multiple Aeschynanthus species and cultivars; this record is restricted to A. radicans.

records.horticulturalType: Mistletoe cactus species; epiphytic tropical cactus
conflicts: The common name mistletoe cactus can be applied to multiple Rhipsalis taxa; this identity is specifically R. baccifera.

records.horticulturalType: Water spinach species; no red/white biotype assigned
conflicts: Kew reports historical alternative taxonomic treatments citing I. reptans; this record follows Kew's accepted I. aquatica. UGA describes red and white phenotypes, but no phenotype or named selection is assigned here.

records.horticulturalType: Black currant species; no named cultivar assigned
conflicts: UMN discusses cultivar-dependent self-fertility and resistance; these traits are not assigned to the species-level identity without a cultivar.

records.horticulturalType: Red currant species/crop; pink and white fruit-color cultivars not individually represented
conflicts: UMN uses Ribes sativum for red, pink and white currants; Kew accepts Ribes rubrum and treats R. sativum as a synonym. Color forms are not separate species identities here.

records.horticulturalType: European gooseberry species; American gooseberries and hybrids excluded
conflicts: Common name gooseberry also covers American Ribes hirtellum and hybrids; this identity is restricted to accepted European species R. uva-crispa.

records.horticulturalType: American gooseberry species; distinct from European R. uva-crispa and hybrids
conflicts: UMN describes American gooseberries as R. hirtellum or hybrids; no hybrid is assigned to this species-level profile.
The cultivar-level source identifies Black Hawk as a black raspberry floricane type; no disease-resistance or quantified performance claim is made.

records.horticulturalType: American elderberry species; cultivar and regional selection unspecified
conflicts: UF/IFAS discusses the historical treatment S. nigra subsp. canadensis, while Kew accepts S. canadensis; regional source material and cultivar performance are not assumed interchangeable.
Commercial flooding is a seasonal management/harvest practice and does not indicate that the species grows permanently submerged.

records.horticulturalType: Parsnip crop species; no named cultivar assigned
conflicts: UMN guidance is for Minnesota home gardens and not cultivar-specific; cultivar dimensions and maturity claims are not assigned.

records.horticulturalType: Rutabaga crop type within B. napus; no cultivar or infraspecific taxon assigned
conflicts: Common crop names and infra-specific treatments for swede/rutabaga vary; this identity is conservatively set at accepted species level with crop type noted separately.

records.horticulturalType: Hyacinth bean species; ornamental use selected, cultivar unspecified
conflicts: The species has edible and ornamental uses, but this record is scoped to ornamental cultivation and does not claim safe preparation of pods or seeds.

records.horticulturalType: Winged bean species; daylength response may vary by cultivar
conflicts: UF/IFAS notes traditional daylength-sensitive types and day-neutral cultivars; no specific cultivar or photoperiod response is assigned here.

records.horticulturalType: Pineapple sage species; named cultivars excluded
conflicts: Extension sources differ in seed-starting recommendations; seed propagation is possible, while selected cultivars are typically retained by cuttings. No cultivar traits are generalized.

records.horticulturalType: Species-level tropical foliage houseplant; cultivars excluded
Accepted epiphytic species; no cultivar assigned
Variable accepted species with multiple accepted subspecies; cultivar Lisa excluded
conflicts: Kew recognizes infraspecific diversity; this identity remains at species level and does not assign a subspecies or the horticultural cultivar Lisa.

records.horticulturalType: Accepted orchid species; commercial Phalaenopsis hybrids excluded
conflicts: The retail Phalaenopsis trade is dominated by complex hybrids; this profile is only the named accepted species.

records.horticulturalType: Accepted species-level tropical houseplant; Tricolor cultivar excluded
Cape primrose/false African violet species; not S. ionanthus
conflicts: Common-name overlap with African violet can cause confusion; the record preserves the separate accepted species S. saxorum.

records.horticulturalType: Species-level stock identity; many commercial stocks are hybrids involving other Matthiola species
conflicts: NC State notes that many sold stock varieties are hybrids, and strict species plants may not be commercially available; this profile does not claim a specific stock cultivar.

records.horticulturalType: Four-o'clock species; flower colors and patterns vary and no cultivar is assigned
conflicts: Common names and flower colors do not identify a named cultivar; vegetative tuber regrowth may preserve an individual plant's characteristics.

records.horticulturalType: Common morning-glory species; named color cultivars excluded
conflicts: The genus Ipomoea includes sweet potato and moonflower; this record is specifically I. purpurea. Regional invasive and seed-toxicity cautions are not generalized beyond evidence.

records.horticulturalType: Garden impatiens species; no color, series or disease-resistance cultivar assigned
conflicts: Commercial garden impatiens include cultivars and series; disease resistance varies, and no cultivar-level performance is claimed.

records.horticulturalType: Cardinal flower species; named cultivar Queen Victoria is not represented
conflicts: This species is distinct from other Lobelia identities; toxic effects are documented for ingestion of plant parts, not ordinary garden contact.
Commercial cultivars vary in height and disease response; no cultivar-specific traits are assigned.

records.horticulturalType: Eastern purple coneflower species; cultivars unspecified
conflicts: Disease resistance is reported for some cultivars only and is not assigned here.

records.horticulturalType: Pale purple coneflower species; cultivar unspecified
conflicts: This species is distinct from E. purpurea and E. tennesseensis; do not transfer their traits.

records.horticulturalType: Ornamental moss rose species; cultivar unspecified
conflicts: Keep distinct from P. oleracea and from named commercial series.

records.horticulturalType: Annual Indian blanket flower species; distinct from perennial G. aristata
conflicts: The common name blanket flower also applies to G. aristata and G. × grandiflora; this record is strictly G. pulchella.

records.horticulturalType: Perennial great blanket flower species; distinct from G. pulchella
conflicts: Commercial G. × grandiflora is a hybrid, not this species identity.
NC State uses catnip, catmint and catswort as common names; no named garden cultivar is implied.

records.horticulturalType: Bay laurel species; not Kalmia or Quercus species also called laurel
conflicts: The common name laurel is used for unrelated genera; this record is limited to Laurus nobilis.

records.horticulturalType: Cultivated pineapple species; no named fruit cultivar assigned
conflicts: The species encompasses diverse cultivars and forms; no commercial cultivar traits are assigned to this generic identity.

records.horticulturalType: French tarragon (var. sativa in Illinois Extension usage), vegetatively maintained culinary type; distinct from Russian tarragon
conflicts: Kew confirms the accepted parent species but does not accept var. sativa among listed infraspecific taxa; Illinois Extension uses Artemisia dracunculus var. sativa for French tarragon. The catalog represents it as a horticultural type and does not reclassify it as a separate species or named cultivar.

records.horticulturalType: Eastern North American wintergreen species; no cultivar assigned
conflicts: Wintergreen and teaberry are common names shared by unrelated plants; this record is restricted to Gaultheria procumbens.
NC State lists named compact cultivars, but none is assigned to this species-level identity.
UF/IFAS describes cultivar-specific variation; no cultivar is selected.

records.horticulturalType: Eastern North American pawpaw; distinct from tropical papaya
conflicts: The common name pawpaw is also used for tropical papaya in some regions; this identity follows the accepted taxon Asimina triloba.

records.horticulturalType: American/common persimmon species; distinct from D. kaki
conflicts: NC State notes usually separate sexes but occasional perfect flowers; sex is not assigned to an unspecified plant.

records.horticulturalType: Asian/Japanese persimmon species; cultivars such as Fuyu and Jiro excluded
conflicts: Fruit astringency and pollination behavior vary by cultivar/tree; no cultivar-specific trait is assigned.

records.horticulturalType: Loquat/Japanese medlar; not Japanese plum Prunus salicina
conflicts: NC State notes Japanese plum is an ambiguous common name also used for Prunus salicina; identity is fixed here by the accepted scientific name.

records.horticulturalType: Hardy kiwi species; sex and cultivar unspecified
conflicts: Several cultivars and three accepted varieties exist; this record is retained at species level and does not identify sex or cultivar.

records.horticulturalType: Red mulberry species; distinct from white mulberry and named selections
conflicts: This is Morus rubra, not a retail white-mulberry hybrid or named fruiting selection.

records.horticulturalType: Common buckwheat; cover-crop use, cultivar unspecified
Crimson clover cover-crop species; cultivar unspecified
White clover species; no lawn cultivar assigned
Cereal rye; cover-crop use, cultivar unspecified
Cultivated oats; cover-crop use, cultivar unspecified
Alpine/woodland strawberry species; not a Fragaria × ananassa cultivar
conflicts: Common-name use overlaps with wild/woodland strawberry; the profile follows species identity Fragaria vesca.
Black chokeberry is distinct from chokecherry, which belongs to Prunus.

records.horticulturalType: Honeyberry/haskap fruit crop; cultivar and subspecies unspecified
conflicts: Cultivar compatibility is required for fruiting; this species record does not identify a compatible pair.
Distinct from Vaccinium macrocarpon (American cranberry), which is separately cataloged.
The cited Extension growing dimensions are genus-level and are not assigned to this species.

records.horticulturalType: Butterfly pea species; flower cultivar unspecified
conflicts: The common name butterfly pea is also used for other species; this identity is specifically Clitoria ternatea.

records.horticulturalType: Mexican oregano / oregano de monte; not Origanum oregano
conflicts: Kew accepts Lippia origanoides and treats Lippia graveolens as a synonym; some regional sources use L. graveolens as an accepted name.

records.horticulturalType: Stalk celery crop type; horticultural distinction from Chinese leaf celery and celeriac; not a named cultivar
conflicts: Kew's current accepted species is Apium graveolens and treats infraspecific names as synonyms; WSU uses var. dulce for the stalk celery crop. This record retains the crop type without elevating it to a separate accepted species.

records.horticulturalType: Chia seed crop; distinct from golden/desert chia Salvia columbariae; no named cultivar
conflicts: Common name chia also refers to Salvia columbariae; this identity is restricted to S. hispanica.

records.horticulturalType: Quinoa/quinua grain species; no seed color, cultivar or landrace assigned
conflicts: WSU reports substantial variety and day-length adaptation differences; grocery grain and unnamed cultivars are not assumed to perform identically.

records.horticulturalType: Grain/ornamental species; distinct from vegetable amaranth Amaranthus tricolor; no cultivar assigned
conflicts: Common name amaranth covers multiple grain, leafy vegetable and ornamental species; this entry is specifically A. hypochondriacus and does not inherit A. tricolor seed-start details.

records.horticulturalType: Accepted species known as Mexican snowball; retail hybrid Echeverias not included
conflicts: Kew accepts Echeveria elegans Rose and treats E. albicans as a synonym; an illegitimate later homonym is treated differently. This catalog follows the accepted Rose name.

records.horticulturalType: Zebra haworthia species; distinct from Haworthiopsis fasciata
conflicts: Retail common name zebra plant is also used for unrelated species; NC State distinguishes H. attenuata from H. fasciata. This record is specifically H. attenuata.

records.horticulturalType: Trailing succulent species; no named cultivar assigned
conflicts: Burro's tail is used for more than one trailing succulent in retail; this entry is limited to S. morganianum.

records.horticulturalType: Common houseleek species; unassigned retail hens-and-chicks hybrids excluded
conflicts: Common name hens and chicks also applies to other Sempervivum and Echeveria taxa; this identity is specifically S. tectorum.

records.horticulturalType: Cornflower/bachelor's button species; flower color and cultivar unspecified
conflicts: Common name bachelor's button can also refer to unrelated plants; identity here is specifically Centaurea cyanus.

records.horticulturalType: Strawflower species; no named cultivar or seed strain assigned
conflicts: NC State notes many named cultivars do not grow true from seed; this entry is species-level and does not imply a cultivar identity.

records.horticulturalType: Sesame/benne crop species; cultivar, seed color and shattering trait unspecified
conflicts: UF/IFAS describes benne as an heirloom sesame type; no benne cultivar or seed color is assigned to this species-level identity.

records.horticulturalType: Purple pitcher plant species; subspecies and horticultural cultivar unspecified
conflicts: Kew recognizes accepted northern and southern subspecies; this profile does not resolve a particular subspecies or cultivated selection.

records.horticulturalType: Sweet William species; color and cultivar series unspecified
conflicts: Common names such as pink and Sweet William can be used broadly; this record follows the accepted species D. barbatus, not other Dianthus species or a named seed strain.

records.horticulturalType: Common hollyhock species; no named cultivar or color strain
conflicts: Kew records Alcea rosea as a cultigen; garden forms vary in lifecycle and dimensions. No cultivar or color identity is assigned.

records.horticulturalType: Common foxglove species; no named cultivar/series assigned
conflicts: Named first-year flowering hybrid series and color selections are excluded; the species-level profile does not inherit their traits.

records.horticulturalType: Annual baby's-breath species; distinct from perennial G. paniculata
conflicts: The common name baby's breath also applies to G. paniculata; this entry is specifically the annual G. elegans species.

records.horticulturalType: Apple species; cultivar and rootstock unspecified
conflicts: Cultivars and rootstocks have distinct horticultural traits; none is assigned to this species-level identity.

records.horticulturalType: European/common pear species; cultivar and rootstock unspecified
conflicts: Common pear may refer broadly to other Pyrus species; this entry is fixed to P. communis.

records.horticulturalType: Asian pear species; cultivar and rootstock unspecified
conflicts: Asian, apple, Chinese and sand pear are common names used for different Pyrus taxa; this record follows P. pyrifolia.

records.horticulturalType: Peach/nectarine species; no named cultivar assigned
conflicts: Peach and nectarine are forms within P. persica; the species profile does not assign a named cultivar or fruit type.

records.horticulturalType: European/common plum species; greengage, damson and prune cultivars not assigned
conflicts: European plum is distinct from Japanese plum P. salicina; subspecies/cultivar identities are not resolved here.
Some common-name sources use Chinese plum; the scientific identity distinguishes this from P. domestica.

records.horticulturalType: Sweet cherry species; cultivar and rootstock unspecified
conflicts: Keep distinct from sour/tart cherry P. cerasus; pollination and size can vary by cultivar/rootstock.

records.horticulturalType: Sour/tart cherry species; named ornamental cultivars excluded
conflicts: Double-flowered ornamental cultivars are not treated as fruit cultivars in this species-level profile.
Common name apricot can include other Prunus taxa; this entry is restricted to P. armeniaca.

records.horticulturalType: Smooth blackberry species; distinct from other Rubus taxa sold as blackberry
conflicts: Blackberry is a broad common name across Rubus; this profile is limited to the accepted taxon R. canadensis.

records.horticulturalType: Celtuce/stem-lettuce crop form; not a named cultivar
conflicts: NC State refers to Lactuca sativa var. augustana for celtuce; this catalog retains accepted species L. sativa and records celtuce as horticultural type rather than a cultivar.

records.horticulturalType: Cultivated flax species; fiber/seed type unspecified
conflicts: Fiber flax and linseed are distinct cultivated forms/uses; this entry does not identify either type.

records.horticulturalType: Cultivated rice species; subspecies and grain type unspecified
conflicts: Rice subspecies and grain groups have meaningful differences; none is assigned to this species-level entry.

records.horticulturalType: Spring barley crop; malting/food/forage cultivar unspecified
conflicts: Spring versus winter habit and malting class are cultivar/crop distinctions; this identity does not claim them beyond the spring-crop evidence cited.
Sorghum includes grain, forage and other crop types; this identity is limited to grain sorghum and does not specify a cultivar.

records.horticulturalType: Proso millet grain species; cultivar unspecified
conflicts: The common name millet covers several distinct species; this identity is specifically proso millet.
Adzuki/azuki identity is distinct from other beans sold as red bean; no regional cultivar is assigned.
Common names vary by region; this entry represents the species and not a named landrace or cultivar.
Common name sorrel applies to unrelated Oxalis and multiple Rumex taxa; this entry is restricted to Rumex scutatus.

records.horticulturalType: Cardoon horticultural form; distinct harvested use from globe artichoke
conflicts: Cardoon and globe artichoke are horticultural forms in the Cynara cardunculus complex; the record preserves the cardoon form and does not assign a named cultivar.
Horseradish is not the common radish Raphanus sativus; common names and edible root use should not merge the identities.

records.horticulturalType: Domesticated edible nopal species; cultivar unspecified
conflicts: Prickly pear is used for many Opuntia species; this entry is specifically O. ficus-indica, not a claim about all prickly pears.
Despite a garlic-like common name and aroma, this is Tulbaghia, not Allium sativum or garlic chives.

records.horticulturalType: Moonflower vine species; not Datura moonflower
conflicts: Moonflower is also used for Datura; this identity is specifically Ipomoea alba.
Pincushion flower is shared by other taxa; this record is limited to Scabiosa atropurpurea.

records.horticulturalType: Sea thrift species; subspecies and cultivar unspecified
conflicts: The source notes geographic subspecies; none is assigned to this identity.
The source records Scabiosa caucasica as a synonym; the accepted profile identity follows Lomelosia caucasica.
Common name wild celery is also used for unrelated plants; accepted name anchors this identity.
Clary sage is distinct from culinary common sage Salvia officinalis.
The documented taproot makes transplant timing important; this is not an indoor-container compatibility claim.
Wild bergamot is distinct from cultivated Monarda hybrids and other species sold as bee balm.

records.horticulturalType: Mexican sunflower species; annual pollinator flower
conflicts: Do not infer compact habit from dwarf cultivars of other Tithonia selections.
The species includes variable forms and cultivars; no flower-color or compactness claim is assigned.

records.horticulturalType: Blue false indigo species; native perennial
conflicts: A deep taproot constrains transplanting; this profile does not imply container suitability.
Distinct from compact Nicotiana × sanderi horticultural hybrids in this catalog.

records.horticulturalType: Common snapdragon species; tall/dwarf horticultural selections not assigned
conflicts: The source lists multiple tall and short cultivars; no named cultivar or cultivar-specific size is assigned.
The selected page is a species identity source and does not support propagation guidance for this entry.

records.horticulturalType: Green columbine species; not genus-wide columbine guidance
conflicts: Species-specific evidence is sparse; genus-level columbine traits are not assigned here.

records.horticulturalType: Nicotiana alata × N. forgetiana hybrid; cultivar unspecified
conflicts: This hybrid is distinct from N. alata; product cultivars and compactness are not specified.

records.horticulturalType: Taro food-crop identity; no named cultivar or horticultural subgroup assigned
conflicts: Common names taro, malanga, dasheen, and elephant ear can refer to other aroids; this identity is specifically Colocasia esculenta.

records.horticulturalType: Cassava/yuca crop species; sweet/bitter type and cultivar unspecified
conflicts: UF/IFAS distinguishes sweet and bitter cyanogenic types; this profile does not resolve type or cultivar and preserves food-safety uncertainty.

records.horticulturalType: Blackeye/southern-pea crop form associated with accepted subsp. unguiculata; cultivar unspecified
conflicts: Common-name use overlaps broadly with cowpea; this identity is scoped to the blackeye/southern-pea crop form and kept distinct from V. unguiculata subsp. sesquipedalis yardlong bean.

records.horticulturalType: Greater galangal culinary species; distinct from lesser galangal and other galangal-named taxa
conflicts: Common names galangal and Thai ginger also refer to other species; this identity is specifically A. galanga.

records.horticulturalType: Common culinary sage species; no named cultivar assigned
conflicts: Common sage is distinct from pineapple sage (Salvia elegans), clary sage (S. sclarea), and named leaf-color cultivars.

records.horticulturalType: Curry-leaf tree species; no named compact or dwarf form assigned
conflicts: Kew accepts Bergera koenigii and lists Murraya koenigii as a synonym; older horticultural and nursery references continue to use the synonym.
